title: The clone-monolith-workflows-secrets policy is not configured with Audit validation
content_excerpt:
The checkout's clone-monolith-workflows-secrets ClusterPolicy is generate-only and does not set validationFailureAction: Audit. Therefore the report's claim that both live ClusterPolicies use Audit validation is not supported by the repository.

## Evidence

- projects/platform/kyverno/templates/clone-monolith-pg-secret-policy.yaml
- projects/platform/kyverno/templates/require-resources-policy....
evidence: projects/platform/kyverno/templates/clone-monolith-pg-secret-policy.yaml:34-63 is generate-only with no validationFailureAction; require-resources-policy.yaml:26 has Audit
rationale: The claim holds, but the note is a rebuttal fragment ('the report's claim') whose subject is missing, and the checkout now has three ClusterPolicies, not the 'both' it alludes to.

title: Context-free graph workflow IDs can collide
content_excerpt:
session_key catches every exception while reading DBOS.workflow_id and falls back to a shared None-prefixed key, so calls outside a workflow can reuse an idempotency key and attach to the same existing agent session.

## Evidence

- projects/monolith/graph/workflows.py:29-40
- projects/monolith/agent_sessions/api.py:23-46
evidence: projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/workflows.py:82-94 catches every exception reading DBOS.workflow_id and returns f'{None}-{suffix}'
rationale: Behaviour is unchanged, but both cited paths are dead after the graph -> swarm -> factory renames, so a reader cannot follow the evidence.

title: Factory delivery plans require independent exact-head review and Linux CI
content_excerpt:
A factory delivery plan includes investigation, implementation, and independent exact-head review, with required Linux CI before completion.

## Evidence

- Turn 1 result: created plan defines investigation → implementation → independent exact-head review and requires passing Linux CI
evidence: factory_conductor.py:180 role enum investigate/implement/review/integrate; review_publisher.py:133 exact-head approval; no rule requires an investigation node per plan
rationale: One plan's shape ('Turn 1 result: created plan defines ...') is generalised into what every delivery plan requires.

title: Base vendor coverage does not prove sibling convergence
content_excerpt:
EmberVM BaseVendorCoverage can remain true when one sibling reports a fresh base and another reports a stale base, because coverage attests vendor build presence while status separately exposes the mixed references.

## Evidence

- git show 7096d4609: BaseVendorCoverage comment and implementation
- projects/embervm/control/test/embervm/base_builder_test.exs: mixed refs with BaseVendorCoverage true
evidence: base_builder_test.exs:5098-5126 asserts BaseVendorCoverage True with mixed refs; base_builder.ex:2123-2135 documents the split
rationale: Precise, commit-anchored, cites both implementation and the test that proves it.

title: Both GKE node pools were spot-backed during the incident
content_excerpt:
On 2026-09-04, both the ember-bricks and workload-n2 pools used n2-standard-8 spot nodes, so the EmberVM control plane and workload tier had no on-demand node floor.

## Evidence

- kubectl get nodes showed both pools with cloud.google.com/gke-spot=true
- kubectl top nodes showed the two n2-standard-8 nodes
evidence: ADR platform/016 (a5e37600d, 2026-09-04) moved core to on-demand the same day; live today: core-e2 e2-standard-8 on-demand, ember-bricks n2-standard-8 spot
rationale: Correct as a dated historical observation, but 'the incident' in the title is never identified and the fix that landed the same day is not linked.

title: Cron cadence changes were applied and governed subsequent runs
content_excerpt:
After ArgoCD synchronized the chart, worldcup-sim stopped firing, home-cluster-snapshot-refresh ran only on even minutes, and observability-stats-rollup ran every five minutes; observed runs in the post-sync window succeeded.

## Evidence

- Live CronWorkflow specs showed worldcup-sim suspended, home-cluster-snapshot-refresh at */2, and observability-stats-rollup at */5
- Post-sync workflow lis...
evidence: projects/monolith/chart/values.yaml: worldcup-sim suspend: true (l.393), home-cluster-snapshot-refresh '*/2' (l.679), observability-stats-rollup '*/5' (l.423)
rationale: Three config facts and a one-off 'observed runs succeeded' are bundled into one note that refers to 'the chart' and 'the post-sync window' without saying which.

title: shortNumber emits billion-scale values with a B suffix
content_excerpt:
When formatting 5238700000 through the factory overview formatter, shortNumber returns "5.2B".

## Evidence

- Node focused assertion output: `focused model assertions passed`
- The assertion checked `shortNumber(5238700000) === "5.2B"`
evidence: projects/monolith/frontend/src/lib/public/factory/model.js:21 returns `${(n / 1e9).toFixed(1)}B`
rationale: A true but near-trivial unit-test fact; the evidence is an assertion message rather than the source path.

title: MTP verify buffers are sized per query token
content_excerpt:
When MTP verification carries multiple query tokens for one request, the attention and graph paths allocate and slice token-indexed buffers by batch size times query width, while recurrent state remains request-indexed.

## Evidence

- git show 95fbe43: commit summary states QSA MTP block tables use token-specific storage and recurrent ring state remains per request
- git show 95fbe43 lists cha...
evidence: commit 95fbe43 is not in this repo and no file named qsa_sparse.py or test_mtp_verify_path.py is tracked; this is the freetoken fork
rationale: Well-written note about another repository filed under repo:jomcgi-org/homelab, so an auditor of this repo cannot check it.

title: The repository commit could not create its worktree lock
content_excerpt:
The attempted conventional commit failed because Git could not create `/Users/jomcgi/repos/homelab/.git/worktrees/toolcall-leak/index.lock`, reporting `Operation not permitted`.

## Evidence

- Tool output [63]: `fatal: Unable to create ... index.lock: Operation not permitted`
evidence: one-off sandbox permission error on a local worktree index.lock; nothing in the checkout to compare
rationale: Records a single failed tool call ('Tool output [63]') on Joe's laptop; it is not knowledge about the system.

title: The AgentTurn model at commit 8902bdc13 stored reported and list cost in separate fields
content_excerpt:
The report claims that the AgentTurn model had distinct cost_usd and list_cost_usd fields rather than a stored cost_source. The cited model lines in the checkout confirm both fields; the cited daily-view migration likewise lacks cost_source. The report also cites issue #5892 being closed, but that issue-state claim was not independently confirmed from checkout.

## Evidence

- git show 8902bdc1...
evidence: git show 8902bdc13:projects/monolith/factory/execution/models.py:199-200 has cost_usd and list_cost_usd, no cost_source; the migration exists at that commit; gh issue 5892 is CLOSED
rationale: Everything it says is true, but it is written as a verifier's running commentary ('The report claims ... not independently confirmed') rather than as a fact.

title: CI test commands can fail before executing tests when Bazel cannot resolve @bazel_gazelle
content_excerpt:
When `ci` or `ci test` reaches the remote runner with an unresolved `@bazel_gazelle` dependency, the command exits with failure before tests execute.

## Evidence

- `ci` remote runner output: `@bazel_gazelle` repository could not be resolved, command exited 1
- `ci test` remote runner output: same Bazel resolution failure before test execution
evidence: MODULE.bazel:38 pins gazelle 0.47.0; the failing runner output is not retrievable
rationale: Near-tautological ('when the dependency is unresolved the command fails') with no cause, date, or reproduction.

title: Deleting an agent session clears bindings only after EmberVM destruction
content_excerpt:
When an agent session has an EmberVM session ID, the delete endpoint destroys that EmberVM session first and then clears its bindings; sessions without an EmberVM ID return an empty result, while transport errors are converted into an error response.

## Evidence

- projects/monolith/agent_sessions/router.py lines 1163-1177: delete_session branches on ember_session_id, destroys before clearing ...
evidence: projects/monolith/factory/execution/router.py:1579-1592 destroys the EmberVM session, then clears bindings, returns {} without an ID, and catches EmberVMTransportError
rationale: Accurate description of the handler, but the cited path (agent_sessions/router.py) no longer exists and the note carries no date.

title: Full conductor tests are blocked by missing dbos dependency
content_excerpt:
When the focused conductor test suite reaches workflow-submission coverage, collection fails because the environment lacks the `dbos` module.

## Evidence

- Pytest traceback: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'dbos'` at `factory_conductor.py:3806`.
evidence: dbos is imported lazily at factory_conductor.py:4649 and :4841; the Bazel test environment provides @pip//dbos, so this describes an ad-hoc local pytest run
rationale: 'The environment' is some unnamed local sandbox; the note generalises a missing pip package into a repo fact.

title: Codex and Pi interrupt adapters do not signal their child processes
content_excerpt:
The Codex and Pi runtime adapters implement `interrupt()` as a no-op, so their running child processes cannot be cancelled even if an interrupt caller is added.

## Evidence

- Raw issue brief for #4321 identifies no-op `interrupt()` implementations at `projects/embervm/runtimes/claude/shim.py:1157` and `:1399`.
evidence: projects/embervm/runtimes/claude/shim.py:3251, :4003, :5144, :5970 implement interrupt() with process lookup and signalling; issue #4321 is CLOSED
rationale: Perfectly clear and fully wrong today: the no-op interrupts were fixed under #4321 and the note was never superseded or given a valid_until.

title: Brick preemption recovery uses three bounded outcomes
content_excerpt:
When an agent turn encounters EmberBrickGone, transport relights banked or parked sessions, restores by lineage when possible, or creates a replacement session with workspace-loss metadata, and bounds recovery using MAX_PENDING_DISPATCHES.

## Evidence

- projects/monolith/agent_sessions/transport.py:1012-1078
- raw transcript: deliver recovery arms and dispatch_count bound
evidence: projects/monolith/factory/execution/transport.py:1756-1812: relight for banked/parked, restore_from=lineage_id, replacement with workspace-loss metadata, bounded by MAX_PENDING_DISPATCHES
rationale: Correct mechanism, dead path (agent_sessions/transport.py), no date.

title: Deleted files map to their nearest surviving Bazel package
content_excerpt:
When a deleted file belongs to a surviving Bazel package, affected-targets.sh maps it to that package's :all label, deduplicates multiple deletions, and skips files outside every package.

## Evidence

- affected_targets_test.sh output: PASS [deleted_package], PASS [deleted_nearest_package], PASS [deleted_outside_package], PASS [deleted_and_changed]
- Final harness result: 33 passed, 0 failed
evidence: bazel/tools/ci/affected-targets.sh:128-129 falls back to //... on any deleted file; git log -S deleted_nearest_package finds no commit, and nothing touched the script on 2026-09-06
rationale: Describes a working-tree change that never merged as if it were the repo's behaviour; the evidence is the session's own test output.
cause_tag: other: unmerged change recorded as fact

title: Token broker network policy admits node sidecars on port 8080
content_excerpt:
The rendered token broker CiliumNetworkPolicy permits endpoints labeled noded and noded-brick to reach the broker on TCP port 8080.

## Evidence

- Rendered policy output listed noded and noded-brick under fromEndpoints and port 8080/TCP
evidence: tokenbroker-networkpolicy.yaml was deleted in ff457206e (2026-09-22, 'remove inert Cilium policy resources'); kubectl get cnp -A shows no broker policy
rationale: True on 2026-08-03, false since 2026-09-22; a dated note with no valid_until that nothing closed when the policy was removed.

title: Volume delete quiet-window timestamps are process-local
content_excerpt:
StatefulManager records each reporting node's manager-clock timestamp during reconcile; because the map is process-local, a control-plane restart requires the full quiet window to elapse again after a subsequent report.

## Evidence

- stateful_manager.ex diff adds node_last_reported_at_ms and updates it from state.clock during reconcile
- implementation comment states the tracking is deliberat...
evidence: projects/embervm/control/lib/embervm/stateful_manager.ex:364-375 ('deliberately process-local'), :2972-2990, :3697
rationale: Names the module, the map, the clock, and the consequence of a restart; matches the code exactly.

title: Services 002 remains superseded with persisted scheduling incomplete
content_excerpt:
The repository architecture records services/002 as deleted and superseded in practice, while persisted scheduled tasks remain unfinished.

## Evidence

- projects/monolith/ARCHITECTURE.md:1176
- projects/monolith/ARCHITECTURE.md:1254
evidence: projects/monolith/ARCHITECTURE.md:1683 (persisted scheduled tasks remain) and :1820 (services/002 deleted, superseded in practice)
rationale: Accurate but 'remains' is a time-sensitive word with no date, and the line numbers have already drifted.

title: One-shot Qwen jobs with EmberVM infrastructure failures do not rerun automatically
content_excerpt:
When a one-shot qwen-drain job fails with an EmberVM infrastructure error, its next_run_at remains unset, so it requires an explicit routine-job trigger to re-enter the queue.

## Evidence

- list-routine-jobs output showed 75 one-shot infrastructure failures with next_run_at null
- trigger-routine-job returned {ok:true} for the retriggers
evidence: projects/monolith/agent/routine_jobs.py:6 and :441: one-shot rows clear next_run_at; trigger_job re-queues
rationale: A durable behaviour of the routine-job store, but cited through an MCP tool output rather than the code that implements it.

title: The requested history replacement was not performed
content_excerpt:
Because the worker refused the requested hard reset and commit, the old second commit remained at HEAD and the replacement stayed as an uncommitted working-tree diff.

## Evidence

- Final git log output still showed 872484b73 above f1264a41f.
- Final git status output showed six modified files.
- Assistant final report stated no new commit SHA and that the orchestrator must perform the history...
evidence: SHAs 872484b73/f1264a41f refer to an unnamed branch in a session worktree; no system claim to check
rationale: A worker refused a git reset in one session; this is delivery log, not knowledge.

title: Ember session invocation fails when the workspace is absent
content_excerpt:
When an Ember session's configured workspace does not exist, session invocation fails with HTTP 503 and an error identifying the missing workspace.

## Evidence

- Raw session result: HTTP 503 Service Unavailable; response body states `workspace does not exist: /workspace/src`
evidence: shim.py:2620 raises StartupError('workspace does not exist'); shim.py:6980-6984 maps StartupError to _send(503, ...)
rationale: Correct and clear, but a near-verbatim duplicate of note 2188358 (its note_id even carries the -2 suffix).

title: Gazelle regeneration can fail on a read-only Go module cache
content_excerpt:
When `ci regen` reaches Gazelle and required Go modules are absent, regeneration fails because Gazelle attempts to write module cache files under the read-only host cache.

## Evidence

- `ci regen` output reported operation-not-permitted errors while downloading Go modules into `/Users/jomcgi/go/pkg/mod/cache/download`.
evidence: sandbox permission error writing /Users/jomcgi/go/pkg/mod; not reproducible from the checkout
rationale: A plausible local-sandbox gotcha stated as a general 'ci regen' failure mode without saying which host or sandbox.

title: Security/007 decision 3 was superseded by STPA security lenses
content_excerpt:
Per-domain prose threat models from security/007 were superseded by STPA security lenses under issue #5294; project security findings are represented as extracted rows in the STPA model.

## Evidence

- docs/security.md:417-425
- docs/security.md:534
- docs/runbooks/threat-model-maintenance.md:6-8
evidence: docs/security.md:497-505 and :613 (decision 3 superseded by STPA lenses, #5294); docs/runbooks/threat-model-maintenance.md:7
rationale: Names the ADR, the decision number, the superseding mechanism and the issue; all three cites still hold.

title: OCaml CI routes C-dependent tests to Linux aarch64
content_excerpt:
The OCaml CI shard selects the linux_aarch64 platform and runs PCRE, tree-sitter, and C++ scanner tests without excluding C-dependent cases.

## Evidence

- buildbuddy.yaml:268-277
- buildbuddy.yaml:279-290
evidence: buildbuddy.yaml:307-323 runs //bazel/ocaml/... with --platforms=//bazel/ocaml/platforms:linux_aarch64 including pcre2 and toycaml tests
rationale: Accurate; line cites have drifted by ~40 lines and nothing anchors when it was observed.

title: Detached ORM attribute access can trigger lazy loading after session closure
content_excerpt:
Accessing unloaded SQLAlchemy ORM attributes after the Session context closes can trigger lazy loading and raise an error, so assertions on those attributes must run while the session is active.

## Evidence

- Raw session user diagnosis: assertions outside Session caused system_prompt access to fail
- store_test.py diff moves both system_prompt assertions inside with Session(engine)
evidence: general SQLAlchemy semantics; projects/monolith/factory/execution/store_test.py:200-214 keeps the system_prompt assertions inside `with Session(engine)`
rationale: A clear, correct library fact; the only question is placement, since it is not specific to this repo.

title: PR #6357 review reported a cold-restore failure when no instance owned the recorded lineage
content_excerpt: The agent report says an independent review of PR #6357 at head 2f062bcbf020e8bb25afd52f38afc794b633af3a found that when the recorded owner node had no fleet facts, the restore path tried dialing by bare node ID and failed as `:unknown_node`, denying cold restore from the object store. The report cites ember-session 10507, review_recover, turn 1, and the PR head. The checkout contains that revi...
evidence: commit 2ee73c5e8 (2026-09-30) 'keep the volume without dialing the bare node when no instance owns a parked lineage'; PR #6357 MERGED
rationale: Everything checks out, but three hedged clauses ('does not independently establish ...') make it a review summary rather than one claim.

title: Watchdog logs retain session identity
content_excerpt:
Structured EmberVM watchdog logs preserve session_id because the log formatter whitelists it as a metadata key.

## Evidence

- log_formatter.ex adds session_id to @meta_keys
- log_formatter_test.exs asserts session_id survives formatting
evidence: projects/embervm/control/lib/embervm/log_formatter.ex:19-23 lists :session_id in @meta_keys; log_formatter_test.exs:142 asserts it survives
rationale: Short, one claim, names the mechanism and the test.

title: ADR 064 was not merged and was rolled into the factory-conductor direction
content_excerpt:
The architecture decision history records ADR agents/064 as proposed in PR #5792, never merged, rolled into the Direction subsection on 2026-09-06, with its full text preserved on issue #5784.

## Evidence

- projects/monolith/ARCHITECTURE.md:731-733
- projects/monolith/ARCHITECTURE.md:845
evidence: projects/monolith/ARCHITECTURE.md:1807 and :1925 (ADR 064 proposed in PR #5792, never merged, rolled into Direction on 2026-09-06, text on #5784)
rationale: Matches the decision-history table word for word.

title: The first build-metadata patch failed on a missing adapter test file
content_excerpt:
The initial BUILD and chart patch failed because it referenced `internal/provider/codexchatgpt/adapter_test.go` before that file existed; the session then retried with a patch that omitted the nonexistent target.

## Evidence

- apply_patch result: "Failed to read .../internal/provider/codexchatgpt/adapter_test.go: No such file or directory"
- The following patch invocation succeeded without th...
evidence: one apply_patch failure in a session; the file internal/provider/codexchatgpt/adapter_test.go question is moot once the patch was retried
rationale: A transient tool error and its retry; nothing here outlives the session.

title: Factory planner replaces an outstanding independent review node
content_excerpt:
When the delivery PR is ready and required Linux checks pass but independent exact-head approval remains outstanding, the factory planner proposes a replacement independent review node.

## Evidence

- Factory task result: PR #6341 remained ready for review, required Linux pr-checks passed, and independent exact-head approval was outstanding.
- Factory task result: planner wrote a decision prop...
evidence: factory_conductor.py:4016-4030 replaces a stalled review/correct node, but the proposal in the note was an LLM planner decision on PR #6341, not a coded rule
rationale: One planner decision on one PR is written as a general conditional about what 'the factory planner' does.

title: Factory attempts that appear sessionless can later complete successfully
content_excerpt:
A factory attempt that had no session and appeared eligible for lost-attempt repair can still be recovered by the existing no_model_post path; receipts 461 and 474 later reached succeeded with failed starts and unresolved_starts equal to zero.

## Evidence

- Production database inspection showed both starts failed with accounting_basis=no_model_post and unresolved_starts=0
- Factory audit time...
evidence: the KG itself: verification_state=invalidated, valid_until=2026-09-20T05:44:42Z, two minutes after valid_from (evidence_corrected)
rationale: Invalidated by its own follow-up within minutes, yet still in the live sampling frame; receipts 461 and 474 mean nothing without the source.

title: Internal trigger retrying depends on endpoint idempotency
content_excerpt:
`_post_internal` documents that POST retries are safe only because its internal trigger endpoints enqueue or start at most one run and treat duplicates as already-running success; future non-idempotent endpoints must not use the helper.

## Evidence

- projects/monolith/app/jobs_main.py:133-141
- Transcript inspection of synthetic and drain endpoint handlers
evidence: projects/monolith/app/jobs_main.py:539-545 docstring says retries are safe only because every caller is idempotent and warns future endpoints off the helper
rationale: Captures the invariant and its boundary in one sentence.

title: The remote CI test command completed successfully
content_excerpt:
When `ci test` ran through the remote Linux/amd64 runner, the command completed with exit code 0 after executing the repository test invocation.

## Evidence

- ci test tool result: exit_code 0
- remote runner output showed the Bazel test invocation and completed without a failure message
evidence: no branch, commit, or target named; `ci test` has exited 0 without running anything (#4118), so exit 0 alone proves nothing
rationale: 'The remote CI test command completed successfully' is a receipt for one run, with no subject.

title: Ember session invocation fails when the requested workspace does not exist
content_excerpt:
When an Ember session is invoked with a workspace path that does not exist, the invocation returns HTTP 503 Service Unavailable with a `workspace does not exist` error.

## Evidence

- Raw session result: HTTP 503 from Ember invocation endpoint; response body states `workspace does not exist: /workspace/src`.
evidence: shim.py:2620 raises StartupError('workspace does not exist'); shim.py:6980-6984 maps StartupError to 503
rationale: Correct and clear; duplicated three days later as 2189395 from a different session.

title: Over-budget reviews retain findings but fail delivery accounting
content_excerpt:
When a review exceeds its node cost cap, the node is marked failed even if its review artifact is valid, and delivery verification ignores the verdict because it only counts succeeded review nodes. The full findings remain in outcome_json.

## Evidence

- swarm_node_run rows for issues 3843, 3855, 3858, and 3907 retained valid artifacts while status was failed
- factory review verification scan...
evidence: factory_controls.py:3375 filters SwarmNodeRun.status == 'succeeded' when collecting the review verdict; graph.py:531 refuses on budget_exceeded; the 'failed with valid artifact' half is a DB observation not checkable from the checkout
rationale: The accounting half is verifiable in code, the failure-mode half rests on four DB rows nobody can re-read.

title: Owner-preserving reconciliation retains workloads after assignment errors
content_excerpt:
When reconcile_assignment/3 encounters an assignment error for a workload that already has a durable owner, it returns :owned_with_assignment_error so the workload remains associated with its durable owner.

## Evidence

- Review of PR 6069: reconcile_assignment/3 returns :owned_with_assignment_error on conflicting assignment errors
evidence: PR #6069 is CLOSED unmerged; grep finds no reconcile_assignment or :owned_with_assignment_error in projects/embervm, and git log -S finds no commit that ever contained it
rationale: A clean, well-cited description of code that never landed: the extractor turned a review of a PR into a fact about the repo.
cause_tag: other: unmerged change recorded as fact

title: OTLP and OTLP/HTTP endpoint syntax are not interchangeable
content_excerpt:
The otlp exporter expects a bare host:port endpoint, while otlphttp expects a URL with a scheme; switching presets without changing the endpoint can leave the collector Ready while exports fail silently.

## Evidence

- git show a86e9a8cd states the two endpoint forms differ
- the session recorded this as a hypothetical failure mode, not a directly observed export failure
evidence: commit a86e9a8cd (2026-08-08) pins the gRPC OTLP exporter; projects/platform/otel-collector/values.yaml:41 uses host:port for otlp; standard collector exporter semantics
rationale: Correct, and honest that the silent-failure consequence was hypothesised rather than observed.

title: The required remote suite passed after the oracle fixes
content_excerpt:
After the dispatcher, checker, and fixture changes, the remote CI test completed with 1301 tests, 0 failures, and 6 skipped.

## Evidence

- /tmp/oracle2.log contained: 1301 tests, 0 failures, 6 skipped
evidence: /tmp/oracle2.log on a laptop; 'the oracle fixes' and 'the dispatcher, checker, and fixture changes' are unnamed
rationale: A test-count receipt from one run with every referent left implicit.

title: Codex turn detects replacement of the mounted workspace identity
content_excerpt:
CodexProcess.turn compares the current workspace identity with the identity captured when the app-server was spawned, and treats a replaced workspace as requiring process remediation even when .codex still exists.

## Evidence

- projects/embervm/runtimes/claude/shim.py:3125-3165
evidence: projects/embervm/runtimes/claude/shim.py:3632-3670 (CodexProcess.turn compares _workspace_identity against the spawn-time value and remediates even when .codex exists)
rationale: Exact behaviour, correct even after the lines drifted ~500 down.
